name: Puligny-Montrachet

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Puligny-Montrachet is a Côte de Beaune commune in Burgundy, and around 99.5% of its production is white wine.
There are four Grand Cru vineyards: Montrachet, Bâtard-Montrachet, Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet and Chevalier-Montrachet.
Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet cross the communal border and are shared with Chassagne-Montrachet.
The Premier Cru climats lie both south of the village toward Chassagne-Montrachet and north toward Meursault.
White Puligny-Montrachet is often very mineral, with more restrained oak than some other Côte de Beaune villages, and is usually described as elegant.

blurb.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making almost only white wine, about 99.5%, from Chardonnay. It has four Grand Cru vineyards, with Montrachet the best known, and 17 Premier Crus.
